key-tree.summary: The key-tree route is entirely inside buildKeyTreeClimb (src/outside.js:1271-1450): a 13-step helical staircase of glowing InstancedMesh balls-on-strings that drop out of the canopy when 'graveyardResolved' fires, invisible flat ramps (world.ramps 'keyTree:0..12') that only exist post-drop, a one-mesh skull-less skeleton at the top tread, and gateKey3 (makeGateKey, outside.js:1455-1508) hovering 0.95 m above it. The balls flicker because they are the only InstancedMeshes in the codebase missing the house idiom `frustumCulled = false`: three r161 caches an InstancedMesh bounding sphere ONCE on the first visible-frame frustum test — while every instance is still seated at CANOPY_Y 9.6 — and never recomputes it, so after the balls descend to y 0.33-5.37 the whole mesh (and the strings mesh) culls out whenever the camera frames the staircase but not the canopy point. The balls answer nothing (no collider, no interactable, no fetch target — a live violation of the answer-a-throw law), while the key itself is a plain swept-sphere fetch target (radius 0.7, outbound-only, no LOS/reach guard, skull.js:1347) sitting north of the bough collider's z-range, so a ground throw fetches it without climbing — the shipped playthrough itself throws for it from step 10. Alex's requested replacement grammar already exists three times over: the bedroom tree's own "branch reaching toward the window with a key on a string" (house.js:1566-1606), the fallen tree's 3-hit staged-collapse fetch target (outside.js:5202-5406), and detachBoard's fall-tumble-settle ticker (main.js:985-1016); the skeleton's put()-list geometry (outside.js:1360-1381) is a ready parts table for fallable bones. Only playthrough.mjs's KEY THREE section (748-780, beats 'the-lights-are-a-staircase' and 'third-key-rides-the-jaw') asserts the climb; regressions.mjs 'gate-takes-three-keys-in-any-order' (1623) is route-agnostic and survives.

key-tree.diagnosis:
FLICKER (Alex: "they come in and out of visibility"): The balls have no act-gating, no LOD, no derived-visibility ticker — nothing in game code toggles balls.visible after drop() (only 1298 false, 1411 true; verified by reading every reference). The cause is Three.js r161 whole-object frustum culling with a stale cached bounding sphere. Vendored three.module.min.js Frustum.intersectsObject prefers object.boundingSphere for InstancedMesh and lazily computes it exactly once (null → computeBoundingSphere over the CURRENT instance matrices), never recomputing when instanceMatrix updates. Invisible objects skip the frustum test, so the first test runs the frame drop() flips visible=true — when every ball is still seated at CANOPY_Y=9.6 (seat(i, CANOPY_Y) at build, outside.js:1317) — caching a ~1.4 m sphere at (5.5, ~9.7, 13.6). The descent then moves the balls to y 0.33-5.37, up to ~9 m outside that sphere, so whenever the camera frames the staircase without the canopy point (standing near the tree looking level/down) the entire 13-ball mesh culls; look up and it pops back. The strings mesh fails identically (cached as 0.05-long stubs at the canopy). The codebase's own fix idiom is `frustumCulled = false` — 18 occurrences, with the explanatory comment at underfalls.js:558 ("unit-geometry bounds sit at the origin") and on the fallen-tree branch InstancedMesh at outside.js:5248 — buildKeyTreeClimb is the one instanced-mesh builder that omits it. (Secondary, distinct, lesser trap: the back-district culler snapshot/restore at outside.js:5126-5137 can stomp a drop() that fires while graveyard roots are hidden — not the in-yard flicker Alex saw, since that hides the whole yard at once, but worth preserving against in the redesign.)
NO INTERACTION ON BALLS: they are registered nowhere — not world.interactables (E-pick), not world.fetchTargets, no world.addCollider — so LMB throws pass clean through and E does nothing; only the invisible treads do anything, and only for feet. This violates the answer-a-throw law and is the other half of Alex's complaint.
THROW-SKIPS-THE-CLIMB: gateKey3's onHit (outside.js:1483-1490) guards only mode==='outbound' && !carry; _checkTargets (skull.js:1347-1365) is a pure swept-segment-vs-sphere with no line-of-sight, occlusion, or thrower-position guard, and the key's 0.7 sphere at ≈(6.15, 6.32, 14.55) sits north of the only bough collider (house.js:1615 spans z 8.6-12.0 only), so a ground throw from the north yard fetches it. The shipped playthrough already legitimizes throw-for-the-key (from step 10, playthrough.mjs:772-774), so 'climb then throw' vs 'stand on grass then throw' differ by zero code — Alex's observation that the key also reads as beside the tree, not on it, is geometrically true: the helix center is 2.1 m north of the trunk axis and the key floats ~1 m below the canopy underside at its northern rim.

gate.diagnosis: TWO distinct findings. (A) The "opened with two keys" is not reproducible in this code: the count is airtight (bank() consumes the single carry; banked keys are derived invisible/disabled at outside.js:1499-1500; restore() only replays 'gateKeyBanked:N' flags that bank() itself set; the ossuary counterweight no longer touches the gate; both flag-guarded openGate callers require 'graveyardCleared' which only fires at banked()>=3; there is no cross-session persistence to import stale state). The evidence says Alex banked three while believing he had two: gateKey2 is silently auto-jawed with the marrow relic (marrow.js:682) — deliberately, per HANDOFF decision #1 — so its acquisition never registers as "getting a key"; additionally the 'gateSockets' fetch target (0.62 radius, live from boot) will bank a carried key on any throw that grazes the lock-stone, e.g. mid-combat. "It looked like three" = the three seated keys in the sockets, which is the correct end state. underfalls-finale.diagnosis:
A) Why the Choir is never seen (verified, not speculative): it is NOT flag-gated off, NOT culled (installCaveVisibility keeps enemy meshes, underfalls.js:1324), NOT count=0, and the aug15 branch did not touch it (git diff ca8ec27..HEAD -- src/director.js src/underfalls.js src/enemies.js contains zero choir/cave hunks; those diffs are frozen-falls/three-routes/PIERCE). The authored trigger DOES fire on the main route: choirTriggerZ = chapel.z+7 = local z61, crossed on the east-ambulatory(z49)→lower-sluice(z62) leg (horror-expansion.mjs:116-139 proves a teleport to lowerSluice spawns it). The compound illegibility: (1) NO choir exists for the first ~60% of the district (veil→throat→apse→pump approach→chapel — the whole showpiece chapel has only the passive displacement figure); (2) it spawns ~3-4m BEHIND the player on the corridor just walked, then stands still through a 2.65s audio-only warning while the player walks on; (3) it pursues heardPos — the player's own breadcrumbs — so it is structurally always in the player's rear 180°; every reveal event (warning→stalk revealT 1.35, drench revealT 1.6, spray) decays in ~1.4s and happens behind the view cone; (4) dry visibility floor is voidMat opacity 0.02 + droplet shader 0.10 in a 0.42-ambient cave — effectively invisible even when looked at; (5) closing speed on a walking player is ~0.7 m/s (3.45 vs 2.7) minus warning, so earliest contact is on the sluice climb, exactly where the |Δy|<0.72 sameReachableSpace gate suppresses pressure across storeys; a running player (4.7 > 4.35 heardSpeed) can never be caught; (6) the player's own spray-curtain crossings fire caveSpray, and if the pursuing choir is inside the zone it gets an 8%-speed wetT slow plus washback — resetting the chase it was winning. Net: audio-only rear pressure the player attributes to ambience. This is the FETCH legibility-law failure mode (working-but-illegible), present since the aug14 build. Other cave-unique enemies: none, ever, in this source — enemy kinds are walker/resident/kneeler/choir; no director cave spawns besides beginDrownedChoir; the second "creature" is buildSprayDisplacement (underfalls.js:1087, explicitly 'not an enemy', passive, relocates only unseen, exits before the upper gallery). Alex's "maybe there was just one before" is correct. Test hole: choir-route-occlusion asserts routing MATH with forced spawns (and disarms the real trigger at its line 81); horror-expansion asserts lifecycle via teleports; playthrough asserts only !g.dead crossing the district; NO test asserts the choir intercepts the player path or achieves a visible reveal inside the view cone.
B) Why the hands don't read as bone: becomeBone is a recolor of the same flesh geometry — tapered overlapping capsule phalanges, webbing sphere, palm/heel spheres, box fingernails, dark sleeves (built at skull.js:321-418 explicitly to read as "the player's living hands, not a second skeleton") — so bone-colored, it reads as a pale glove, exactly Alex's complaint; the recolor also uses only M.bone.color (plain MeshStandardMaterial, no bone texture/bump applied), and in the mirror act the viewmodel key runs at ~23% intensity (act 0.6^1.25 × 'gone' carried 0.44, main.js:1252-1264) with a warm tint, further muddying it. Why the raise reads late/never: raiseHands(7) fires only inside _beginContact — the last 2.35s before hard black, simultaneous with pane flares, the lunging reflection, and the recall moan; the goneBlend damp (2.2) spends ~1s just bringing the hands above the visibility threshold (g<0.985, skull.js:573), so fully-raised bone hands exist on screen for roughly one second. Worse: through the whole multi-ten-second 'closing' phase the glass-press beat (_updatePressure) poses hands that are INVISIBLE, because mode==='gone' keeps g≈1 and nothing raises them until contact. Donor search result: no articulated skeletal hand mesh exists anywhere in the codebase — searched outside.js (tree skeleton: capsule arms, NO hands), finale.js (reflection hand: capsule glove, miniature), enemies.js (WALKER_BONE_MAT only), textures.js (M.bone material only), marrow.js/house.js via bone greps. The fix therefore needs new phalanx geometry grafted onto the EXISTING mkFinger k1/k2 rig (which is the frozen animation contract) plus the M.bone material family.
